keyQuotes: Purple Bird Browser's revenue share dropped from 97.4% in 2023 to 84.1% in 2025 — not because it couldn't sell, but because they acquired Zhanfu.
A company that emphasizes 'AI R&D capability' as a key fundraising focus actually saw its RMB intensity decline over the past three years.
Is this an underrated cash machine, or an overvalued AI story?

mainPoints.explanation: In 2025, Purple Bird Browser accounted for 84.1% of total revenue, while AI product LinkFox contributed only 2.5%. AI is the core narrative in the prospectus, but the profit source remains the legacy product, and R&D intensity has actually declined.
mainPoints.point: Purple Technology's revenue is highly dependent on the seven-year-old Purple Bird Browser, with AI products accounting for a minimal share.

mainPoints.explanation: Operating profit was 257 million RMB and operating cash flow was 364 million RMB, but net profit was only 57.49 million RMB due to non-cash fluctuations from redeemable liabilities. Upon successful IPO, liabilities will convert to equity, and negative net assets will disappear.
mainPoints.point: The company's low book net profit and negative net assets are an accounting illusion; its real profitability is strong.

mainPoints.explanation: Purple Bird subscribers grew from 186,000 to 416,000, but ARPU dropped 11%, net revenue retention fell from 125% to 117%, and renewal rate declined from 92.5% to 90.3%, putting pressure on unit economics.
mainPoints.point: Growth relies on volume and acquisitions, with ARPU, retention rate, and renewal rate all declining simultaneously.

mainPoints.explanation: The company has ample cash flow yet allocated large sums to wealth management and dividends, contrasting with the stated fundraising purposes. Declining R&D intensity also weakens the credibility of the AI narrative.
mainPoints.point: Pre-IPO rush dividend of 240 million RMB and hoarding of 600 million RMB in wealth management products raise questions about fundraising motives.

oneSentenceSummary: This article deeply dissects Purple Technology's IPO prospectus, revealing core contradictions: heavy revenue reliance on the seven-year-old Purple Bird browser, minimal AI story contribution, growth driven by volume and acquisitions, and pre-IPO dividend rush.
originalTitle: 「紫鸟浏览器」冲港股 IPO，两位草根创始人逆袭的暴利故事
summary: Based on Purple Technology's (Purple Bird Browser) Hong Kong IPO prospectus, this article breaks down its financial and business substance one by one. Data shows that out of total revenue of 687 million RMB in 2025, Purple Bird Browser contributed 84.1%, while AI product LinkFox accounted for only 2.5%; operating profit was 257 million RMB and operating cash flow was 364 million RMB, but net profit was only 57.49 million RMB, mainly due to redeemable liability book fluctuations. ARPU, retention rate, and renewal rate all declined year by year, with growth relying on new subscriber volume and the acquisition of Zhanfu Browser. Before the IPO, the company distributed 240 million RMB in dividends in a rush and hoarded 600 million RMB in wealth management products, while R&D intensity actually declined. Founder Yang Jinhe came from a seller background, and the team scrambled to build a governance structure before going public. The article argues that the company is essentially an 'anti-detect browser' business, with a gap between AI narrative and investment, and highlights risks deeply tied to platform policies.
title: Purple Bird Browser's Hong Kong IPO: A Profitable Story of Two Grassroots Founders' Rise
